item.title: US denies Iran's claim it downed warplane near Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Thursday claimed it intercepted and destroyed an advanced warplane belonging to the United States and Israel south of Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, according to a statement carried by Iranian media. The IRGC said the aircraft crashed into Gulf waters after being struck by its air defense systems, though no details were provided about the type of aircraft or its crew. Iranian state television broadcast footage it said showed the moment the warplane was hit.

US Central Command swiftly rejected the claim. "All U.S. fighter aircraft are accounted for. Iran's IRGC has made the same false claim at least half a dozen times," CENTCOM said in a post on X.

item.title: Half of Iran's missile launchers intact after weeks of strikes, assessment finds
item.description:
A new U.S. intelligence assessment indicates that roughly half of Iran's missile launchers remain intact and thousands of one-way attack drones are still in its arsenal after five weeks of intensive American and Israeli airstrikes, according to CNN. The findings directly undercut repeated claims by President Trump and senior officials that Iran's military capabilities have been all but eliminated since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.

In a national address on April 1, Trump told Americans that Iran's "missiles are just about used up or beaten," adding that "their navy is gone, their air force is gone". Earlier, on his Truth Social account, Trump declared that "Iran has been, essentially, decimated". Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has cited a 90 percent drop in Iranian missile launches since the start of the conflict.

item.title: South Korea, France elevate ties to strategic partnership
item.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and French President Emmanuel Macron elevated their countries' relationship to a "global strategic partnership" on Friday following summit talks in Seoul, marking the most notable overhaul of bilateral ties in more than two decades.

The upgrade replaces a "comprehensive partnership for the 21st century" that had been in place since 2004. It comes as the two nations celebrate the 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations and seek closer alignment on defense, energy security, and advanced technology amid what French officials described as "significant international and regional tensions".

item.title: Trump's April 6 deadline for Iran nears as 40 nations seek Hormuz deal
item.description: More than five weeks into the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, the conflict's economic toll is spreading well beyond oil markets, choking off a third of the world's helium supply and prompting governments from Europe to Southeast Asia to accelerate their pivot toward renewable energy.

item.title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery again, sparking fires
item.description: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery early Friday, igniting fires across several operational units in the latest assault on Gulf energy infrastructure since the U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran began in late February.

item.title: Artemis II crew heads to the moon after successful engine burn
item.description: Four astronauts are hurtling toward the moon aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft after a successful launch and a critical engine burn sent them out of Earth orbit, marking the first crewed voyage beyond low Earth orbit in more than half a century.

item.title: Global food prices jump for second straight month as Middle East war disrupts supply chains
item.description:
Global food commodity prices rose for a second consecutive month in March, climbing 2.4 percent as the escalating conflict in the Middle East sent energy and fertilizer costs surging through agricultural supply chains, according to data released Friday by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 128.5 points in March, up from a revised 125.5 in February. The increase marks the sharpest monthly jump in the index since mid-2025 and follows February's 0.9 percent rise, which had ended a five-month streak of declines.

item.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel and Gulf states as war enters sixth week
item.description: Iran launched a fresh barrage of missiles at Israel and several Gulf nations on Friday as explosions rocked Tehran and the central Iranian city of Isfahan, marking an intensifying cycle of strikes as the five-week-old war showed no signs of abating.

item.title: CMA CGM ship becomes first Western European vessel to cross Hormuz since Iran war
item.description:
A container ship owned by France's CMA CGM has exited the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first known transit by a vessel linked to Western Europe since the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran all but shuttered the vital waterway in late February.

The Maltese-flagged CMA CGM Kribi sailed from waters off Dubai on Thursday afternoon local time, broadcasting "owner France" on its transponder system as it navigated a channel between the Iranian islands of Qeshm and Larak, according to Bloomberg. By Friday morning, the vessel signaled it was off Muscat, Oman. The ship is believed to be heading toward Pointe Noire in the Republic of Congo as part of a service linking India, the Middle East Gulf, and Africa.

item.title: China's Tianlong-3 rocket fails on maiden flight
item.description: China's most powerful privately developed rocket, the Tianlong-3, failed on its debut flight on Friday after experiencing an anomaly mid-flight, dealing a setback to the country's ambitions to rapidly deploy satellite megaconstellations rivaling SpaceX's Starlink.

item.title: Iran claims capture of US pilot after F-15E allegedly downed
item.description:
Unconfirmed reports emerged on Friday suggesting that the pilot of a U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle may have been captured by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps after the aircraft was apparently shot down over Iranian territory, marking what would be the first known loss of a crewed American fighter jet over Iran since the start of Operation Epic Fury.

Iranian state media initially claimed on April 3 that IRGC air defenses had destroyed a second U.S. F-35 stealth fighter over central Iran. However, images from the crash site — showing the remains of a vertical stabilizer bearing markings consistent with the 494th Fighter Squadron, part of the 48th Fighter Wing based at RAF Lakenheath in the United Kingdom — indicate the aircraft was an F-15E Strike Eagle, not an F-35.

item.title: Rescue operation unfolds as debris in Iran identified as U.S. F-15E
item.description: Images of fighter jet wreckage surfaced on Iranian state media on Friday, April 3, as independent analysts identified the debris as belonging to a U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle — not the F-35 stealth jet Iran initially claimed to have downed. Geolocated footage from southern Iran simultaneously revealed an American combat search-and-rescue operation underway deep inside Iranian territory, in what could mark the first confirmed loss of a crewed U.S. aircraft over Iran since the start of Operation Epic Fury on February 28.

item.title: Artemis II crew shares first photos of Earth from deep space
item.description: NASA released the first images downlinked from the Artemis II astronauts on Friday, revealing Earth in vivid detail as the crew races toward the Moon on the first human lunar voyage in more than half a century.

item.title: Trump says Israel will halt Iran war on his orders
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared that Israel would halt its military campaign against Iran on his orders, asserting his personal authority over the course of the five-week-old conflict in an interview with TIME magazine published on Thursday.

"They'll do what I tell them," Trump said of the Israelis. "They've been a good team player. They'll stop when I stop. They'll stop unless they're provoked, in which case, they'll have no choice, but they'll stop when I stop."

The remarks, made in a phone call with TIME on the morning of April 2, came hours after Trump threatened further escalation in the war in a post on Truth Social. "Our Military… hasn't even started destroying what's left in Iran. Bridges next, then Electric Power Plants!" he wrote, adding that Iran's "New Regime leadership knows what has to be done, and has to be done, FAST!"

item.title: IDF says disarming Hezbollah 'not a goal' of Lebanon campaign
item.description:
The Israeli military said Friday that it has struck more than 3,500 targets across Lebanon in the month since fighting with Hezbollah erupted on March 2, a figure that underscores the scale of Israel's air and ground campaign against the Iran-backed militia.

The targets include weapons depots, rocket and missile launch sites, command centers, and anti-tank missile positions, according to the IDF. The military also said it has killed approximately 1,000 Hezbollah operatives since hostilities began, including hundreds of members of the group's elite Radwan Force.

item.title: U.S. F-15E shot down over Iran; one crew member rescued
item.description: A U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over southwestern Iran on Friday, and one of its two crew members has been rescued by American forces, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News. The loss marks the first confirmed shootdown of a manned American combat aircraft by enemy fire since the U.S.-Iran war began on February 28.

item.title: Macron calls for 'coalition of independence' against US and China
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday urged democratic nations to form a "coalition of independence" to resist the dominance of both the United States and China, delivering a pointed address to students at Yonsei University in Seoul during his first visit to South Korea in over a decade.

"Our objective is not to be the vassals of two hegemonic powers," Macron said, warning countries against falling under China's "dominance" while also shielding themselves from what he called the "unpredictability" of the United States. He proposed an alliance of middle powers including European nations, Japan, South Korea, Brazil, Canada, and India — countries he said share commitments to democracy and international law.

item.title: UN says Iran war is accelerating global renewable energy shift
item.description: The month-old U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has triggered the largest oil supply disruption in history, and analysts say the crisis is now accelerating a global pivot toward renewable energy as countries scramble to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels funneled through vulnerable chokepoints.

item.title: UN delays vote on Hormuz shipping resolution to Saturday
item.description:
The United Nations Security Council on Friday postponed a vote on a Bahrain-led draft resolution that would authorize the use of "defensive" force to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, with diplomats indicating a new vote could take place as early as Saturday, April 4.

The vote had been scheduled for Friday morning but was pushed back on the grounds that the UN observes Good Friday as a public holiday — a fact that was already known when the vote was initially planned. Some diplomatic sources said no firm new date had been set, though Reuters and other outlets reported Saturday as the likely target.

item.title: UN delays Hormuz vote to Saturday after stripping military enforcement powers
item.description:
India finds itself at the center of one of the most consequential diplomatic standoffs of the Gulf conflict, threading a needle between its Western partners, its BRICS allies, and its own energy security interests as the United Nations Security Council prepares to vote on a Bahrain-drafted resolution to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The vote, initially expected Friday, has been pushed to Saturday due to the Good Friday holiday at the UN. The final text, now stripped of its original Chapter VII enforcement authority after six successive drafts over 15 days, authorizes member states to use "all defensive means necessary and commensurate with the circumstances" to secure passage through the strait — but explicitly rules out offensive military action.
